A pack over the size ceiling
results.evidence: `pack_too_large` is raised at source line 90 and `self._zip(members)` runs at line 89 — the whole archive is built, compressed and held in memory before its size is measured against the 2GB ceiling. Every member is already resident as bytes in `members` too, so the peak is the uncompressed content plus the archive. The refusal protects the recipient from an export nobody can open; it does not prot

results.title: A pack requesting a document kind that does not exist
Two attachments with the same filename and a colliding digest prefix
results.evidence: two attachments named 'report.pdf' whose digests agree on bytes 7:15 produced 1 archive member(s) — ['attachments/AAAAAAAA-report.pdf'] — while attachments/index.json lists 2. The name is `digest[7:15] + filename`, a dict assignment overwrites, and no gap is recorded: the index says two documents are in this pack and one of them is not. 0 gap(s) recorded

results.title: A share created with `max_reads: 0`
results.evidence: `max_reads: 0` was stored as None: the guard is `if max_reads`, and zero is falsy, so asking for NO permitted reads produces a share with NO LIMIT — the exact inverse of the request, and the one direction that cannot be noticed by reading the row back

results.title: A share created with `max_reads: -1`
results.evidence: `max_reads: -1` was accepted and the share is born exhausted: nothing validates the field, so a typo produces a link that refuses every read and reads on the register as one somebody used up
